obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N81-R03)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data: checkout page skimming, a tampered or substituted terminal, or card numbers exposed from notes
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the acquirer, not law. Other brands' rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the acquirer immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Acquirer; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the acquirer. Other brands as the acquirer directs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the acquirer opens a case; other brands' rules were not verified
clock_starts: Suspicion or confirmation of the compromise

obligation: Manufacturer A notice of suspected customer data incident (contractual)
citation: Manufacturer A authorized service provider agreement (fictional term)
trigger: Suspected incident involving customer data or devices handled under the program (for example a technician copying device content at a Manufacturer A store)
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (program agreement term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Partner P1 and P2 breach notice (contractual)
trigger: Breach or suspected breach of partner claim data (for example through the partner API, SYS-01, or a technician)
deadline: Within 48 hours of discovery (partner agreement term)
notify: Partner security contact named in each agreement
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: Company as third-party agent: notice to the partner (statutory)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(1)(h), (6)(a) (N81-R02); author interpretation, counsel to confirm
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a partner (claim data held as the partner's agent)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the company must give the partner all information it needs to notify. The 48-hour contract term is shorter and controls in practice
notify: Partner (the covered entity), which then notifies individuals and regulators unless it asks the company to notify on its behalf (6)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for claim data of Florida residents; other states' laws have similar agent duties (counsel checks)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Business account contract notice (contractual)
trigger: Incident affecting a business account's devices or data
deadline: Within 72 hours of confirmation (contract term)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the affected accounts - contractual

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with medical, biometric, or geolocation information, a name with a card number plus any required code, and an email address or user name with a password (501.171(1)(g)). Good-faith employee access for a business purpose is not a breach (501.171(1)(a)); snooping or copying is not good faith
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days only for this notice if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days, 501.171(3)(a)). Notice by mail or email ((4)(d)) with the content in (4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for exported credential notes, lab data exposure, or checkout skimming; counsel decides for single-device content
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred
owner: Privacy and Compliance Manager with counsel

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice to individuals would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in its written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested (for example a police investigation of a technician)

obligation: Florida no-notice determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep for at least 5 years, and provide to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for a contained single-device case with no copies; counsel decides
owner: Privacy and Compliance Manager with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to notice to individuals, not to this notice). Content listed in (3)(b)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents (likely for an SYS-01 export, lab exposure, or checkout skimming)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
owner: Privacy and Compliance Manager with counsel

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (15 U.S.C. 1681a(p)): timing, distribution, and content of the notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (SYS-01 vendor, cloud provider, contact center platform, chatbot or diagnostics vendor, payment gateway) has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: No later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the agent must give the company the information it needs to notify
notify: The company (Security Manager and General Counsel); then the company's own notices apply
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts (POAM-009)

obligation: State data breach notification (other states)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48) (N81-R02)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - mail-in customers, checkout customers, and partner claimants live in every state; counsel applies each state's law to the affected list by state
owner: General Counsel with outside breach counsel

obligation: HIPAA business associate breach notice to a covered entity (conditional)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held as a business associate, only if counsel finds that a business associate relationship arose (for example the 2 dental practice data recovery cases in 2026, P03 G-149)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected - the company declines covered entity work; listed so the case is not missed
owner: Privacy and Compliance Manager with counsel

obligation: Report to law enforcement
trigger: Suspected theft of customer data or devices by a workforce member; skimming or account compromise; extortion
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0-2); coordinate with counsel before contacting police about an employee
notify: Local police (insider theft); FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office (card data or account compromise)
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy: use the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company extends no consumer credit and is not a financial institution under Part 314 (P03 G-147)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size; the company exceeds its SBA size standard, so counsel assesses sector coverage if a final rule is published

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
